concepts.explanation: Mediation holds the middle of a discussion: summarise each side in your own words — Vega dice que…, César pide que… — ask for clarification when a line crosses, repair the misunderstanding before proposing, and only then offer a way forward (propongo que… / podríamos…). The repair frames no te sigo and ¿puedes repetir? work the same way they did at B1; the new move is the two-sides summary before the proposal.

examples.target: Vega dice que la calle debería ser peatonal por las tardes.
examples.meaning: Vega says the street should be pedestrian in the afternoons.

examples.target: César pide una hora de descarga por la mañana.
examples.meaning: César asks for one loading hour in the morning.

examples.target: Por un lado, el barrio gana en calma; por otro lado, el reparto necesita su horario.
examples.meaning: On the one hand the neighbourhood gains calm; on the other, the deliveries need their schedule.

examples.target: Perdona, ¿puedes repetir lo de la descarga?
examples.meaning: Sorry, could you repeat what you said about the unloading?

examples.target: Propongo que la calle abra sin coches por las tardes.
examples.meaning: I propose that the street open without cars in the afternoons.

concepts.commonError: Proposing before summarising: a mediation that skips the two-sides summary leaves the other person unheard — first name both positions, then propose.

concepts.title: Un argumento con contrapunto
concepts.explanation: A written argument holds its position and answers the other side: the stance frame opens it (en mi opinión, creo que), porque carries each reason, aunque acknowledges the strongest counterpoint, and the contrastive connector (sin embargo, en cambio) answers it. The reader should see both a clear position and a real counterpoint handled — conceding a point makes the argument stronger, not weaker.

examples.target: En mi opinión, el centro debería ser peatonal por la tarde.
examples.meaning: In my opinion, the centre should be pedestrian in the afternoon.

examples.target: Creo que la plaza ganaría en vida, porque la gente pasea sin ruido.
examples.meaning: I think the square would gain life, because people stroll without noise.

examples.target: Aunque el reparto se complica, una hora de descarga lo resuelve.
examples.meaning: Although delivery gets harder, one loading hour solves it.

examples.target: Sin embargo, sin horarios claros, el problema vuelve.
examples.meaning: However, without clear schedules, the problem comes back.

examples.target: En cambio, los comercios ganan clientes que pasean.
examples.meaning: By contrast, the shops gain customers who stroll.

concepts.commonError: Naming the counterpoint and giving up: acknowledging the other side with aunque is a move, not a surrender — the answer after the counter (sin embargo, en cambio) is what closes the argument.

concepts.title: Defender una postura en voz alta
concepts.explanation: An argued take spoken aloud follows the same beats as the written one: the stance frame opens it, porque carries the reasons, aunque concedes a point, and the contrastive connector answers it. For a voice note, the signposts do more work — the listener cannot re-read, so la cuestión es… and en resumen hold the take together from the first line to the close.

examples.target: La cuestión es que la calle puede ganar sin que nadie pierda del todo.
examples.meaning: The thing is that the street can win without anyone losing completely.

examples.target: En mi opinión, la calle peatonal merece la pena.
examples.meaning: In my opinion, the pedestrian street is worth it.

examples.target: Aunque el reparto se complica, el horario lo arregla.
examples.meaning: Although deliveries get harder, the schedule fixes it.

examples.target: Sin embargo, sin una hora de descarga, el comercio sufre.
examples.meaning: However, without a loading hour, the shops suffer.

examples.target: En resumen, los dos lados ceden y los dos ganan.
examples.meaning: In short, both sides give ground and both win.

concepts.commonError: Speaking without the signposts: a voice note has no re-read button — en mi opinión, la cuestión es que… and en resumen are the handles that keep the listener on the take.

vocabulary.example: Todo recto, luego a la izquierda.
Todo recto, luego a la izquierda.
La mesa está en la cocina.

vocabulary.meaning: I/he/she was going / used to go

vocabulary.example: Todos los días iba al parque.
El fin de semana fue genial.
Por la tarde leí un libro.
Quiero que me digas la verdad.
El tren se retrasó media hora.
Hubo un problema en las vías.
La cancelación del vuelo nos sorprendió.
La portavoz explicó el nuevo horario.
Habría que confirmar el nuevo horario.
Hay que confirmar la nueva reserva.
He oído un aviso por megafonía.
El embarque es a las siete y cuarto.
La puerta es la número doce.
Falta una hora para el vuelo.
Tengo una reunión importante el lunes.
Le envío la confirmación por correo.
El viaje a la costa fue un desastre.
La facturación empezaba a las siete.
Voy a solicitar el puesto de editor.
El curso de diseño empieza en octubre.
Me llaman por una oferta de trabajo.
El sueldo es de mil ochocientos euros.
La editorial es la más conocida.
El sueldo no lo es todo.
La formación me importa más que el dinero.
El horario de la editorial es fijo.
Primero voy a terminar el curso.
Voy a terminar el curso en junio.
Hoy tengo una entrevista de trabajo.
El puesto es de redactor joven.
Quisiera saber más sobre el equipo.
Espero que el equipo sea acogedor.
Llevo dos años de becaria en una revista.
Me gusta la película porque es divertida.
El concierto empieza a las nueve.
Hay una exposición de fotos en el museo.
El museo está tranquilo por la tarde.

stimuli.translation:
As a kid I used to play football.
It was night.
There were many people.

stimuli.body:
Iba a la escuela a pie.
Jugaba al tenis de niño.
Solía correr por las mañanas.
stimuli.translation:
I used to walk to school.
I used to play tennis as a kid.
I used to run in the mornings.

stimuli.body: From «Getting around»: ir — to go · el coche — the car · el metro — the subway · a pie — on foot · el autobús — the bus
From «Numbers and quantities»: uno–cinco · seis–diez · ¿Cuánto cuesta? — how much does it cost? · una manzana — one apple
From «Food and drink»: la comida — the meal · el agua — the water · el pan — the bread · la fruta — the fruit · el queso — the cheese · me gusta — I like
From «Yesterday»: ayer — yesterday · anoche — last night · hablé — I spoke · comí — I ate · fue — it was / he went

From «Formar el pretérito»: trabajé — I worked · comimos — we ate · estuvo — he was · tuve — I had · hice — I did · dijo — he said || From «El imperfecto»: era — it was · iba — used to go · jugaba — used to play · había — there was · quería — wanted · solía — used to
From «Polite requests»: poder — to be able to · querer — to want · querría — I would like · la ayuda — the help · el favor — the favour

pairs.meaning: First I bought the tickets.
Then we waited on the platform.
Afterwards the train arrived.
In the end we had dinner at home.

stimuli.body: Primero fui a la estación con mi hermana. Eran las seis y media y había mucha gente esperando. Luego vimos en la pantalla que el tren de las siete llevaba retraso: hubo un problema en las vías. Mi hermana perdió la paciencia y yo me fui a comprar café. Después vino un aviso: el tren saldría a las ocho. Al final llegamos a casa de nuestros tíos a las diez, pero la cena estaba fría.
stimuli.translation: First I went to the station with my sister. It was half past six and lots of people were waiting. Then we saw on the screen that the seven o'clock train was delayed: there was a problem on the tracks. My sister lost patience and I went to buy coffee. Afterwards an announcement came: the train would leave at eight. In the end we reached our aunt and uncle's house at ten, but the dinner was cold.

stimuli.body:
— Buenas tardes. Me gustaría cambiar mi vuelo a Valencia.
— Claro. ¿Por qué lo quiere cambiar?
— Porque tengo una reunión importante el lunes.
— Entendido. ¿Le importaría viajar el martes por la mañana?
— El martes me va bien, gracias.
stimuli.translation:
— Good afternoon. I would like to change my flight to Valencia.
— Of course. Why do you want to change it?
— Because I have an important meeting on Monday.
— Understood. Would you mind travelling on Tuesday morning?
— Tuesday works for me, thank you.

stimuli.body: El viaje a la costa fue un desastre. Primero salimos tarde de casa porque el despertador no sonó. Luego perdimos el tren de las nueve y esperamos dos horas en la estación. Después tomamos un autobús que llegó con retraso. Al final llegamos al hotel a medianoche, pero la habitación era preciosa.
stimuli.translation: The trip to the coast was a disaster. First we left home late because the alarm clock did not ring. Then we missed the nine o'clock train and waited two hours at the station. Afterwards we took a bus that arrived late. In the end we reached the hotel at midnight, but the room was lovely.

stimuli.body:
You are at the claims desk of the airline. Your flight arrived four hours late and you lost a day of your trip. Your mission:
— Greet and state your purpose: Buenos días. Quisiera reclamar una indemnización.
— Report what happened: Me dijeron que el vuelo salía a las nueve, pero salió a la una.
— Give the consequence: Perdí una noche de hotel.
— Ask what happens next: ¿Cuánto tiempo tarda la respuesta?
— Close politely: Muchas gracias por su ayuda.
stimuli.translation: Estás en el mostrador de reclamaciones de la aerolínea. Tu vuelo llegó con cuatro horas de retraso y perdiste un día de tu viaje. Tu misión: saludar y decir tu propósito, contar lo que pasó, dar la consecuencia, preguntar cuánto tarda la respuesta y despedirte con cortesía.

pairs.target: El año que viene voy a estudiar enfermería.
pairs.meaning: Next year I'm going to study nursing.

pairs.target: Las clases de inglés empiezan a las nueve.
pairs.meaning: The English classes start at nine.
Afterwards I'll work in a hospital.

pairs.target: Estudio enfermería porque me gusta ayudar.
pairs.meaning: I'm studying nursing because I like helping.

stimuli.body: Ana termina el instituto en junio. El año que viene va a estudiar enfermería en Salamanca porque quiere trabajar en un hospital. Las clases empiezan en septiembre, pero antes participa en un curso de verano. Después trabajará en el hospital de su ciudad, si todo va bien.
stimuli.translation: Ana finishes school in June. Next year she's going to study nursing in Salamanca because she wants to work in a hospital. The classes start in September, but before that she takes part in a summer course. Afterwards she'll work in her city's hospital, if all goes well.

pairs.target: El puesto de la editorial es más seguro que el de la agencia.
pairs.meaning: The publishing house post is more secure than the agency one.
You should compare the two offers.

pairs.target: Prefiero la agencia porque el equipo es pequeño.
pairs.meaning: I prefer the agency because the team is small.

pairs.target: Primero voy a terminar el curso.
pairs.meaning: First I'm going to finish the course.
Afterwards I'll apply for the scholarship.

pairs.target: Al final trabajaré en Madrid porque allí hay más oportunidades.
pairs.meaning: In the end I'll work in Madrid because there are more opportunities there.

stimuli.body: Mi plan para el año que viene es claro. Primero voy a terminar el curso de diseño gráfico. Luego solicitaré una beca en el centro de estudios de Valencia. Al final buscaré trabajo en una agencia porque me encanta el diseño publicitario.
stimuli.translation: My plan for next year is clear. First I'm going to finish the graphic design course. Afterwards I'll apply for a scholarship at the study centre in Valencia. In the end I'll look for work at an agency because I love advertising design.

stimuli.body:
You are in a job interview for a junior editor post at a small magazine. Your mission:
— Introduce yourself: Me llamo Lucía y soy de Zaragoza.
— State your experience: Llevo dos años de becaria en una revista.
— Make a polite request: Quisiera saber más sobre el equipo.
— State a hope: Espero que el equipo sea acogedor.
— Close politely: Muchas gracias por la entrevista.
stimuli.translation: Estás en una entrevista de trabajo para un puesto de redactora joven en una revista pequeña. Tu misión: presentarte, decir tu experiencia, pedir con cortesía, expresar un deseo y despedirte con amabilidad.

pairs.target: Me gusta el cine porque las historias me emocionan.
pairs.meaning: I like the cinema because the stories move me.

pairs.target: Me gustan las películas de aventuras.
pairs.meaning: I like adventure films.

pairs.target: ¿Por qué prefieres el museo? — Porque está tranquilo.
pairs.meaning: Why do you prefer the museum? — Because it is quiet.
I'm not coming because of work.

stimuli.body: A Sara le gusta el cine porque las historias le emocionan. A Leo le gustan más los conciertos porque le encanta la música en directo. El sábado no se ponen de acuerdo: «¿Por qué no vamos al cine?», pregunta Sara. «Porque el cine está lejos», responde Leo. Al final van a la exposición de fotos porque es lo único que aceptan los dos.
stimuli.translation: Sara likes the cinema because the stories move her. Leo prefers concerts because he loves live music. On Saturday they cannot agree: 'Why don't we go to the cinema?' asks Sara. 'Because the cinema is far away,' replies Leo. In the end they go to the photography exhibition because it is the only thing they both accept.

pairs.meaning: We're going to celebrate it on Saturday.

pairs.target: ¿Quedamos en la plaza a las ocho?
pairs.meaning: Shall we meet at the square at eight?

pairs.target: ¿Qué te parece si vamos al cine?
pairs.meaning: What do you think about going to the cinema?

pairs.target: Lo siento, no puedo el sábado.
pairs.meaning: I'm sorry, I can't on Saturday.

pairs.target: Prefiero el parque porque es tranquilo.
pairs.meaning: I prefer the park because it is quiet.
I would like to celebrate it at home.

pairs.target: Quedamos en la fuente a las seis.
pairs.meaning: We'll meet at the fountain at six.
Why don't we celebrate on Saturday?

stimuli.body: Mi decisión para mi cumpleaños es sencilla. Prefiero celebrarlo en el parque porque el restaurante es muy caro y el parque es tranquilo. Invito a mis amigos con un mensaje claro: «¿Qué os parece si quedamos en la fuente a las seis?». Al final llevamos la comida y la sorpresa, y no gastamos demasiado.
stimuli.translation: My decision for my birthday is simple. I prefer to celebrate it in the park because the restaurant is very expensive and the park is quiet. I invite my friends with a clear message: 'What do you think about meeting at the fountain at six?' In the end we bring the food and the surprise, and we do not spend too much.

stimuli.body:
You are in a group chat organising a gift for Andrés's birthday, then you run the shop errand. Your mission:
— Propose the gift: ¿Qué os parece si compramos un libro de fotografía?
— Name the aim: El libro es para regalar a Andrés.
— Name the occasion: Compramos el libro por su cumpleaños.
— Organise the money: Ponemos diez euros cada uno.
— Fix the errand: Se lo compro esta tarde en la tienda.
stimuli.translation: Estás en un chat de grupo organizando un regalo para el cumpleaños de Andrés y después haces el recado en la tienda. Tu misión: proponer el regalo, decir el objetivo con para, decir la ocasión con por, organizar el dinero y fijar el recado.

pairs.meaning: While I waited, I read the paper.

pairs.target: Cuando llegó el tren, salimos corriendo.
pairs.meaning: When the train arrived, we ran out.

pairs.target: Primero compré los billetes; luego busqué el andén.
pairs.meaning: First I bought the tickets; then I found the platform.

pairs.target: Al final llegamos tarde, pero todo salió bien.
pairs.meaning: In the end we arrived late, but everything went well.
Although it was raining, we walked.

stimuli.body: Primero bajé al andén y esperé el tren de las ocho. Mientras esperaba, sonaba la música de la emisora y la gente leía en los bancos. Cuando llegó el tren, todos subimos de prisa. Más tarde, en el vagón, sonó mi móvil: era Pablo. Al final llegué a casa muy tarde, pero la cena me esperaba caliente. Aunque no había dormido mucho, me sentía contento.
stimuli.translation: First I went down to the platform and waited for the eight o'clock train. While I waited, the station radio played and people read on the benches. When the train arrived, we all got on quickly. Later, in the carriage, my phone rang: it was Pablo. In the end I got home very late, but dinner was waiting for me warm. Although I had not slept much, I felt happy.

pairs.target: Me dijo que el tren salía a las siete.
pairs.meaning: He told me the train left at seven.

pairs.target: Le dije que esperaría en el andén.
pairs.meaning: I told him I would wait on the platform.
While we waited, it was raining.

pairs.target: No vino porque leyó mal el mensaje.
pairs.meaning: He did not come because he misread the message.

stimuli.body: El sábado quedé con Leo para ir al cine. Me dijo que la sala nueva estaba en la calle Mayor, delante de la estación. Cuando llegué, no había nadie en la entrada. Mientras esperaba, me llamó Leo: «¿Dónde estás?». Le dije que esperaba en la calle Mayor, delante de la estación. «¡Ah! —respondió—, yo estoy en el cine de la plaza: había dos cines en la calle Mayor y me equivoqué de sala.». Al final resultó que los dos fuimos a la misma calle, pero cada uno a un cine distinto. Vimos la película por separado y al día siguiente nos contamos la misma historia.
stimuli.translation: On Saturday I agreed to go to the cinema with Leo. He told me the new screen was on Mayor Street, in front of the station. When I arrived, there was nobody at the entrance. While I waited, Leo called me: 'Where are you?' I told him I was waiting on Mayor Street, in front of the station. 'Ah! —he answered—, I am at the cinema in the square: there were two cinemas on Mayor Street and I got the wrong one.' In the end it turned out that we had both gone to the same street, but each to a different cinema. We watched the film separately and the next day we told each other the same story.

pairs.target: ¿En serio? No me lo puedo creer.
pairs.meaning: Really? I can't believe it.
That's intense! And what happened next?
And what did you do when you saw it?

pairs.target: Fui a casa, aunque estaba cansado.
pairs.meaning: I went home, although I was tired.
First I went to the bakery.
Then I walked back home.

pairs.target: Al final llegué tarde, porque el autobús no pasaba.
pairs.meaning: In the end I was late, because the bus was not coming.

pairs.target: Pero la tarde fue buena igualmente.
pairs.meaning: But the afternoon was good all the same.

stimuli.body: Mi sábado fue sencillo. Primero fui a la panadería y compré pan. Luego volví a casa andando, porque el día estaba bonito. Al final llegué a tiempo para comer con mi familia. Pero hubo una sorpresa: mi hermano trajo un perro nuevo, y la comida se alargó hasta las cinco.
stimuli.translation: My Saturday was simple. First I went to the bakery and bought bread. Then I walked home, because the day was lovely. In the end I arrived in time to eat with my family. But there was a surprise: my brother brought a new dog, and the meal stretched until five.

stimuli.body:
You have recorded a voice note for your friend Nora, who missed your Saturday story. Your mission:
— Open the retell: ¿Te cuento lo del sábado?
— State the event: Perdí el tren de las seis y media.
— Say what you had to do: Tuve que esperar en la estación.
— Give the twist: Al final resultó que mi viaje era el domingo.
— Close with a reaction: ¡Qué suerte que me acordé a tiempo!
stimuli.translation: Has grabado una nota de voz para tu amiga Nora, que se perdió tu historia del sábado. Tu misión: abrir el relato, contar el evento, decir lo que tuviste que hacer, dar el giro y cerrar con una reacción.

pairs.target: Llueve, por eso llevo el paraguas.
pairs.meaning: It's raining, that's why I take the umbrella.

pairs.target: Perdí el tren, así que llegué tarde.
pairs.meaning: I missed the train, so I arrived late.

pairs.target: No había autobuses, entonces fuimos andando.
pairs.meaning: There were no buses, so we walked.

stimuli.body: El sábado Darío tiene que llegar a las doce a la estación. Sale de casa a las diez, porque quiere evitar el tráfico. Por eso lleva el desayuno para comer en el tren. Piensa llegar pronto, así que compró el billete por internet. Al final todo sale bien: llega con media hora de margen.
stimuli.translation: On Saturday Darío has to be at the station by twelve. He leaves home at ten, because he wants to avoid the traffic. That's why he takes breakfast to eat on the train. He plans to arrive early, so he bought the ticket online. In the end everything works out: he arrives with half an hour to spare.

pairs.target: Pensaba que el tren salía a las siete.
pairs.meaning: I thought the train left at seven.
In the end we changed our plans.

pairs.target: Llovía, por eso lo dejamos para otro día.
pairs.meaning: It was raining, that's why we put it off for another day.

stimuli.body: Íbamos a ir a un concierto el sábado. Pensaba que empezaba a las ocho, pero el viernes la organización avisó de que se trasladaba al pabellón cubierto, porque había aviso de lluvia. Al principio nos dio pena, por eso pensamos en quedarnos en casa. Al final fuimos igualmente y salió todo muy bien.
stimuli.translation: We were going to a concert on Saturday. I thought it started at eight, but on Friday the organisers announced that it was moving to the covered hall, because rain was forecast. At first we were sorry, which is why we thought about staying home. In the end we went anyway and it all turned out very well.

pairs.target: Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa.
pairs.meaning: If it rains, we'll stay at home.

pairs.target: Si hace bueno, vamos a ir al parque.
pairs.meaning: If the weather's nice, we're going to the park.
What if it rains?

stimuli.body: El sábado no sabemos qué tiempo hará. Si hace bueno, iremos a la playa y comeremos allí. Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa viendo una película. Por eso tenemos los dos planes preparados: decidimos el sábado por la mañana.
stimuli.translation: On Saturday we don't know what the weather will be like. If the weather's nice, we'll go to the beach and eat there. If it rains, we'll stay at home watching a film. That's why we have both plans ready: we decide on Saturday morning.

pairs.meaning: How about we go to the cinema?
Better we stay at home.
We'll leave it for another day.

stimuli.body: —Sara, ¿qué tal si vamos al museo el sábado? —Uf, el sábado por la mañana no puedo: trabajo hasta las dos. —¿Y si vamos por la tarde? —Mejor: nos quedamos en el centro y luego cenamos juntos. —¡Trato hecho! Lo dejamos para el sábado por la tarde.
stimuli.translation: —Sara, how about we go to the museum on Saturday? —Ugh, Saturday morning I can't: I work until two. —What if we go in the afternoon? —Better: we'll stay in the centre and then have dinner together. —Deal! We'll leave it for Saturday afternoon.

pairs.target: Voy a madrugar, por eso llegaré a tiempo.
pairs.meaning: I'll get up early, that's why I'll be on time.

pairs.target: Salgo con tiempo porque odio las prisas.
pairs.meaning: I leave with time to spare because I hate rushing.

pairs.target: Primero preparo la mochila; luego salgo.
pairs.meaning: First I pack my bag; then I leave.

stimuli.body: El sábado tengo cita con el dentista a las nueve. Voy a madrugar, porque odio las prisas. Por eso preparo la mochila la noche anterior y dejo todo listo. Salgo con tiempo, así que llegaré tranquilo.
stimuli.translation: On Saturday I have a dentist appointment at nine. I'm going to get up early, because I hate rushing. That's why I pack my bag the night before and leave everything ready. I leave with time to spare, so I'll arrive calm.

stimuli.body:
You are organising the group picnic for Saturday, and the forecast mentions possible rain. Your mission:
— Propose the outdoor plan: ¿Qué tal si hacemos un picnic en el parque?
— Add the weather backstop with si: ¿Y si llueve? Pues al café.
— Give the decision with its consequence: Podemos llevarlo todo al aire libre, por eso no hace falta cancelar.
— Keep the re-planning polite with podríamos: Podríamos dejar el picnic para el domingo.
stimuli.translation: Organizas el picnic del grupo para el sábado y el pronóstico menciona posible lluvia. Tu misión: proponer el plan al aire libre, añadir el plan B con si, dar la decisión con su consecuencia y mantener el replanteamiento cortés con podríamos.

pairs.target: Creo que el cine del barrio debería seguir abierto.
pairs.meaning: I think the neighbourhood cinema should stay open.

pairs.target: Me parece que las entradas son caras.
pairs.meaning: It seems to me the tickets are expensive.

pairs.target: Pienso que podemos ir el viernes, porque no hay clase.
pairs.meaning: I think we can go on Friday, because there is no class.

pairs.target: No creo que sea una buena idea cerrarlo.
pairs.meaning: I don't think it's a good idea to close it.

stimuli.body: En el grupo de la clase discuten si el cine del barrio debe seguir abierto. Ana escribe: «Creo que el cine debe seguir abierto, porque es el único sitio barato para ver películas». Luis responde: «Pienso que el cine está viejo, pero me parece que el barrio lo necesita». Carmen añade al final: «No creo que sea buena idea cerrarlo sin preguntar a los vecinos».
stimuli.translation: In the class group they are debating whether the neighbourhood cinema should stay open. Ana writes: 'I think the cinema should stay open, because it is the only cheap place to watch films.' Luis answers: 'I think the cinema is old, but it seems to me the neighbourhood needs it.' Carmen adds at the end: 'I don't think it is a good idea to close it without asking the neighbours.'

pairs.meaning: I agree with you.

pairs.target: De acuerdo, quedamos a las cinco.
pairs.meaning: Agreed, we'll meet at five.

pairs.target: No estoy seguro de que sea tan fácil.
pairs.meaning: I'm not sure it's that easy.

pairs.target: Estoy de acuerdo, porque así ganamos tiempo.
pairs.meaning: I agree, because that way we save time.

stimuli.body: Leo y Nuria deciden dónde desayunar. —¿Qué tal el café de la esquina? —Estoy de acuerdo, porque así ganamos tiempo. —Tienes razón: además, el café es bueno y no está caro. —No estoy seguro del café, pero la terraza me gusta. —De acuerdo, pues al café de la esquina.
stimuli.translation: Leo and Nuria decide where to have breakfast. — What about the café on the corner? — I agree, because that way we save time. — You're right: besides, the coffee is good and not expensive. — I'm not sure about the coffee, but I like the terrace. — Agreed, then the café on the corner it is.

pairs.target: Creo que el regalo de todos es mejor, porque así es más especial.
pairs.meaning: I think a present from everyone is better, because that makes it more special.

pairs.target: No estoy seguro de que le guste el libro.
pairs.meaning: I'm not sure she'll like the book.

pairs.target: Tienes razón en preguntarle a su hermana.
pairs.meaning: You're right to ask her sister.

pairs.target: No creo que sea mala idea preguntar antes.
pairs.meaning: I don't think it's a bad idea to ask first.

stimuli.body: —¿Qué le regalamos a Carmen? —Creo que un regalo de todos es mejor, porque así es más especial. —No estoy seguro de que le guste el libro. —Tienes razón en preguntar; pero a ver: le encanta leer y el cine, así que me parece que un libro y una tarde de cine es el plan. —Me parece bien. No creo que sea mala idea preguntarle a su hermana antes.
stimuli.translation: — What shall we give Carmen? — I think a present from everyone is better, because that makes it more special. — I'm not sure she'll like the book. — You're right to ask; but let's see: she loves reading and the cinema, so it seems to me that a book and a cinema afternoon is the plan. — That seems fine to me. I don't think it's a bad idea to ask her sister first.

pairs.target: En mi opinión, el libro es estupendo.
pairs.meaning: In my opinion, the book is excellent.

pairs.target: Creo que la película vale la pena, porque la historia engancha.
pairs.meaning: I think the film is worth it, because the story grips you.
Also, the music is lovely.

pairs.target: Por ejemplo, yo la vi dos veces.
pairs.meaning: For example, I saw it twice.

stimuli.body: Hola Sara: en mi opinión, el plan del sábado es estupendo. Creo que la película vale la pena, porque la historia engancha. Además, podemos ir todos juntos, y por ejemplo los niños están invitados. En fin, yo voy seguro.
stimuli.translation: Hi Sara: in my opinion, Saturday's plan is excellent. I think the film is worth it, because the story grips you. Also, we can all go together, and for example the children are invited. Anyway, I'm definitely going.

stimuli.body:
A friend has just moved to your town and asks you for a recommendation: a place to eat, a film or a plan for Saturday. Your mission:
— Give your recommendation with a frame: Me parece que… or En mi opinión…
— Add the reason: porque…
— Support it with a detail: además… or por ejemplo…
— Say what it is for: es perfecto para…
— Close warmly: Te lo recomiendo.
stimuli.translation: Un amigo acaba de mudarse a tu ciudad y te pide una recomendación: un sitio para comer, una película o un plan para el sábado. Tu misión: dar la recomendación con un marco, añadir la razón con porque, apoyarla con un detalle con además o por ejemplo, decir para qué sirve con es perfecto para y cerrar con calidez con te lo recomiendo.

stimuli.body: En el grupo de la casa comparten los problemas de la semana. Sara escribe: «Se ha estropeado la lavadora y mañana tengo que lavar la ropa de los niños». Leo contesta: «El wifi tampoco funciona desde ayer, y el técnico no me ha llamado». Marta añade: «Hay un problema con la ducha: el agua sale muy fría». Al final, Iker propone: «¿Me podría alguien hablar con el administrador para arreglarlo todo el mismo día?».
stimuli.translation: In the house group they share the week's problems. Sara writes: 'The washing machine has broken down and tomorrow I have to wash the children's clothes.' Leo answers: 'The wifi isn't working either since yesterday, and the technician hasn't called me.' Marta adds: 'There's a problem with the shower: the water comes out very cold.' In the end, Iker proposes: 'Could someone talk to the building manager to get it all fixed the same day?'

pairs.meaning: The washing machine has broken down.

pairs.target: El wifi no funciona desde ayer.
pairs.meaning: The wifi hasn't worked since yesterday.

pairs.target: Hay un problema con la ducha.
pairs.meaning: There's a problem with the shower.

pairs.target: La nevera funciona mal: enfría muy poco.
pairs.meaning: The fridge works badly: it cools very little.

pairs.target: ¿Me podría enviar a alguien esta semana?
pairs.meaning: Could you send someone this week?

stimuli.body: Leo habla con la administración del edificio por el ascensor. —¿Me podría enviar a alguien esta semana? Hay que arreglar el ascensor, porque no funciona bien. —Claro, le doy el teléfono del técnico. ¿Le vale el jueves? —Me vale si vienen por la mañana. —Pues queda el jueves a las diez, y es mejor avisar al técnico esta misma tarde.
stimuli.translation: Leo talks to the building management about the lift. — Could you send someone this week? The lift has to be fixed, because it doesn't work well. — Of course, I'll give you the technician's number. Does Thursday work for you? — It works for me if they come in the morning. — Then it's set for Thursday at ten, and it's better to notify the technician this very afternoon.

pairs.target: ¿Me podría enviar a alguien esta semana?
pairs.meaning: Could you send someone this week?
The lift has to be fixed.

pairs.target: Hay que cambiar la correa de la lavadora.
pairs.meaning: The washing machine belt has to be replaced.

pairs.target: Hay que avisar al técnico esta misma tarde.
pairs.meaning: The technician has to be notified this very afternoon.

pairs.target: Me vale si vienen por la mañana.
pairs.meaning: It works for me if they come in the morning.

stimuli.body: Lucía habla con el administrador por la lavadora de la comunidad. —¿Me podría enviar a alguien esta semana? La lavadora se ha estropeado. —Claro. ¿Qué tal si va el técnico el jueves? —Mejor por la mañana, porque estoy en casa. —Pues nos quedamos en el jueves a las diez. —Perfecto, nos quedamos en eso. Perdona, ¿me repite la hora? —A las diez de la mañana, el jueves.
stimuli.translation: Lucía talks to the building administrator about the shared washing machine. — Could you send someone this week? The washing machine has broken down. — Of course. What if the technician goes on Thursday? — Better in the morning, because I'll be at home. — Then we settle on Thursday at ten. — Perfect, we settle on that. Sorry, can you repeat the time? — Ten in the morning, Thursday.

pairs.target: ¿Qué tal si va el técnico el jueves?
pairs.meaning: What if the technician goes on Thursday?

pairs.target: Mejor por la mañana, porque estoy en casa.
pairs.meaning: Better in the morning, because I'm at home.

pairs.target: Nos quedamos en el jueves a las diez.
pairs.meaning: We settle on Thursday at ten.
Sorry, can you repeat the time?

stimuli.body: Hola, José: le escribo porque hay un problema con la lavadora de casa. Primero dejó de centrifugar y luego empezó a hacer un ruido raro. Por eso no puedo lavar la ropa aquí. Al final decidí escribirle para pedir una solución. ¿Me podría enviar a alguien esta semana? Gracias.
stimuli.translation: Hi José: I'm writing because there is a problem with the washing machine at home. First it stopped spinning and then it started making a strange noise. That's why I can't wash my clothes here. In the end I decided to write to you to ask for a solution. Could you send someone this week? Thanks.

pairs.target: Hay un problema con la lavadora de casa.
pairs.meaning: There's a problem with the washing machine at home.

pairs.target: Primero dejó de centrifugar y luego empezó a hacer ruido.
pairs.meaning: First it stopped spinning and then it started making noise.

pairs.target: Por eso no puedo lavar la ropa aquí.
pairs.meaning: That's why I can't wash my clothes here.

pairs.target: ¿Me podría enviar a alguien esta semana?
pairs.meaning: Could you send someone this week?

stimuli.body:
You have booked the repair on the phone: the technician visits Thursday morning to fix the washing machine. Now you leave a voice-note message for your landlord. Your mission:
— Open with the reason: Llamo porque…
— Name the problem: Se ha estropeado / No funciona…
— Report the agreement: Al final, nos quedamos en…
— Say what the visit is for: es para / para + the fix
— Close warmly: Gracias por todo.
stimuli.translation: Has concertado el arreglo por teléfono: el técnico visita el jueves por la mañana para arreglar la lavadora. Ahora dejas un mensaje de voz para tu casero. Tu misión: abrir con la razón con llamo porque, nombrar el problema con se ha estropeado o no funciona, contar el acuerdo con al final, nos quedamos en, decir para qué es la visita con es para o para + el arreglo y cerrar con calidez con gracias por todo.

pairs.target: En primer lugar, quiero hablar del horario.
pairs.meaning: First of all, I want to talk about the timetable.

pairs.target: Por un lado es caro, por otro lado es muy bueno.
pairs.meaning: On the one hand it is expensive, on the other hand it is very good.
Then we move on to the second topic.
In the end, everything worked out well.

pairs.target: O sea, que el plan sigue en pie.
pairs.meaning: I mean, the plan is still on.

stimuli.body: En la reunión del barrio, Leo resume el plan de la huerta. «En primer lugar, quiero hablar del horario de los sábados. Por un lado, la mayoría puede venir por la mañana; por otro lado, algunos prefieren la tarde. Luego, hablamos de los materiales, y al final decidimos empezar en mayo. Es decir, que el plan sigue en pie, y o sea, que nos toca organizarnos bien.»
stimuli.translation: At the neighbourhood meeting, Leo sums up the vegetable garden plan.

pairs.target: Según el autor, la idea es clara.
pairs.meaning: According to the author, the idea is clear.

pairs.target: La idea principal es que la biblioteca reabre.
pairs.meaning: The main idea is that the library is reopening.

pairs.target: La biblioteca reabre porque terminaron las obras.
pairs.meaning: The library reopens because the works have finished.
The roof had leaks.
The volunteers painted the rooms.

stimuli.body: Según el autor, la biblioteca cerró porque el tejado tenía goteras y el agua estropeaba los libros. Después de dos años de obras, el edificio reabre en marzo. Los voluntarios pintaron las salas, y la sala infantil estrena estanterías nuevas. La idea principal es que la biblioteca vuelve a ser el centro del barrio.
stimuli.translation: According to the author, the library closed because the roof had leaks and the water was damaging the books. After two years of works, the building reopens in March. The volunteers painted the rooms, and the children's room has brand-new shelves. The main idea is that the library once again becomes the centre of the neighbourhood.

pairs.meaning: Sorry, I'm not following you.
What do you mean by 'leaks'?

pairs.target: Es decir que el agua pasaba por el tejado.
pairs.meaning: That is to say, the water came through the roof.
Sorry, could you repeat the question?
Now it's clear to me.

stimuli.body: Dani y Nuria repasan la crónica de la biblioteca. —Oye, ¿me cuentas la idea principal en dos líneas? —Claro: la biblioteca reabre porque terminaron las obras del tejado. —Perdona, no te sigo con lo del tejado: ¿el tejado o la crónica? —Es decir que el tejado tenía goteras y por eso cerró. —Ah, ahora sí me queda claro.
stimuli.translation: Dani and Nuria go over the library chronicle. — Hey, can you tell me the main idea in two lines? — Sure: the library is reopening because the roof works have finished. — Sorry, I'm not following you on the roof: the roof or the chronicle? — That is to say, the roof had leaks and that's why it closed. — Ah, now it's clear to me.

pairs.target: La idea principal es que la biblioteca reabre.
pairs.meaning: The main idea is that the library is reopening.

pairs.target: Según la crónica, la idea es clara.
pairs.meaning: According to the chronicle, the idea is clear.
Besides, they painted the rooms.

pairs.target: Por ejemplo, la sala infantil tiene mesas nuevas.
pairs.meaning: For example, the children's room has new tables.

stimuli.body: La crónica del barrio cierra con el balance de la reapertura: «La idea principal es que la biblioteca vuelve a ser el centro del barrio. Además, los voluntarios pintaron las salas y la sala infantil estrena estanterías. Por ejemplo, el club de lectura vuelve a reunirse los miércoles».
stimuli.translation: The neighbourhood chronicle closes with the balance of the reopening: 'The main idea is that the library once again becomes the centre of the neighbourhood. Besides, the volunteers painted the rooms and the children's room has brand-new shelves. For example, the reading club meets again on Wednesdays.'

stimuli.body:
You listened to Marta's talk about the neighbourhood vegetable garden, and your friend Leo missed it. Now you leave him a voice note that relays the gist. Your mission:
— Name the source: He escuchado una charla sobre… / Según Marta…
— Give the main point: La idea principal es…
— Add two details: Por un lado…, por otro lado… / Además…
— Reformulate once: O sea, que…
— Close with a reaction: ¡Qué ganas de empezar!
stimuli.translation: Has escuchado la charla de Marta sobre la huerta del barrio, y tu amigo Leo se la ha perdido. Ahora le dejas una nota de voz que transmite lo esencial. Tu misión: nombrar la fuente con he escuchado una charla sobre o según Marta, dar la idea principal con la idea principal es, añadir dos detalles con por un lado, por otro lado o además, reformular una vez con o sea, que y cerrar con una reacción con ¡qué ganas de empezar!

stimuli.body: En fin, para resumir: montamos la huerta en el solar, empezamos en mayo y cada familia cuida una parcela. Os podéis apuntar en la entrada del centro cívico hasta el viernes. Y como decía al principio, lo importante es empezar. ¡Os espero allí!
stimuli.translation: Anyway, to sum up: we set up the garden on the plot, we start in May and each family cares for its own bed. You can sign up at the entrance of the community centre until Friday. And as I was saying at the start, what matters is to begin. I'll see you there!

pairs.target: Creo que el barrio gana con la calle peatonal.
pairs.meaning: I think the neighbourhood gains from the pedestrian street.

pairs.target: Aunque el piso es pequeño, la luz lo compensa.
pairs.meaning: Even though the flat is small, the light makes up for it.
Even if it rained, we would still go out.

pairs.target: Sin embargo, el comercio no va a cerrar.
pairs.meaning: However, the shops are not going to close.

pairs.target: En cambio, la plaza se llenó de terrazas.
pairs.meaning: By contrast, the square filled up with terraces.

stimuli.body: En la reunión del barrio, Vega defiende la calle peatonal. «Aunque perdemos algo de tráfico, el barrio gana en seguridad y en silencio. Creo que las terrazas llenarían la plaza por la tarde. Por un lado, los niños caminan tranquilos; por otro lado, el ruido baja de golpe.» César, el dueño de la papelería, responde: «Sin embargo, mis clientes llegan en coche y necesitan aparcar cerca. No obstante, si la descarga tiene una hora por la mañana, el reparto sigue funcionando. En cambio, cerrar la calle sin horarios sería un error.»
stimuli.translation: At the neighbourhood meeting, Vega defends the pedestrian street. 'Although we lose some traffic, the neighbourhood gains in safety and quiet. I think the terraces would fill the square in the afternoon. On the one hand, the children walk calmly; on the other hand, the noise drops at once.' César, the owner of the stationery shop, replies: 'However, my customers come by car and need to park nearby. Nevertheless, if the loading has one hour in the morning, the deliveries keep working. By contrast, closing the street with no schedule would be a mistake.'

stimuli.body: Parece que el acuerdo está cerca: una hora de descarga por la mañana, terrazas hasta las once y la calle sin coches por las tardes. César lo resume: «En cambio, con horarios claros, ganamos todos.» Vega cierra: «Pues parece que nos hemos puesto de acuerdo.»
stimuli.translation: It seems the agreement is close: one loading hour in the morning, terraces until eleven and the street without cars in the afternoons. César sums it up: 'By contrast, with clear schedules, we all win.' Vega closes: 'Well, it seems we have reached an agreement.'

pairs.target: Según Vega, la calle peatonal vale la pena.
pairs.meaning: According to Vega, the pedestrian street is worth it.

pairs.target: Sin embargo, los clientes mayores llegan en coche.
pairs.meaning: However, elderly customers come by car.

pairs.target: En cambio, sin esos acuerdos, perdería clientes.
pairs.meaning: By contrast, without those agreements, he would lose customers.

pairs.target: Al final, los dos lados ceden un poco.
pairs.meaning: In the end, both sides give ground a little.

pairs.target: La conclusión es que todos ganan algo.
pairs.meaning: The conclusion is that everyone gains something.

stimuli.body: Según Vega, la peatonalización de la calle vale la pena. En primer lugar, los niños caminan tranquilos cuando no pasan coches. En segundo lugar, las terrazas llenan la plaza por la tarde y el barrio se conoce mejor. Vega concede que el reparto se complica, pero cree que con una hora de descarga el problema se resuelve. César, el dueño de la papelería, ve el mismo plan por el otro lado. Sin embargo, los clientes mayores llegan en coche y no quieren caminar con las bolsas de la compra. No obstante, César no pide cerrar el debate: pide un horario fijo de descarga y plazas cortas de aparcamiento cerca de las tiendas. En cambio, sin esos acuerdos, la calle peatonal le haría perder clientes. La conclusión del artículo es que un debate gana cuando cada lado concede algo.
stimuli.translation: According to Vega, making the street pedestrian is worth it. First, the children walk calmly when no cars pass. Second, the terraces fill the square in the afternoon and the neighbourhood gets to know itself better. Vega concedes that the deliveries get harder, but believes that one loading hour solves the problem. César, the owner of the stationery shop, sees the same plan from the other side. However, elderly customers come by car and do not want to walk with the shopping bags. Nevertheless, César does not ask to close the debate: he asks for a fixed loading schedule and short parking spaces near the shops. By contrast, without those agreements, the pedestrian street would cost him customers. The conclusion of the article is that a debate wins when each side concedes something.

pairs.target: Vega dice que la calle debería ser peatonal por las tardes.
pairs.meaning: Vega says the street should be pedestrian in the afternoons.

pairs.target: César pide una hora de descarga por la mañana.
pairs.meaning: César asks for one loading hour in the morning.

pairs.target: Por un lado, el barrio gana en calma; por otro lado, el reparto necesita su horario.
pairs.meaning: On the one hand the neighbourhood gains calm; on the other, the deliveries need their schedule.

pairs.target: Perdona, ¿puedes repetir lo de la descarga?
pairs.meaning: Sorry, could you repeat what you said about the unloading?

pairs.target: Propongo que la calle abra sin coches por las tardes.
pairs.meaning: I propose that the street open without cars in the afternoons.

stimuli.body: En la escalera del barrio, Vega y César discuten la calle peatonal. Vega dice que la calle debería ser peatonal por las tardes: los niños juegan tranquilos y las terrazas se llenan. César pide una hora de descarga por la mañana y plazas cortas de aparcamiento para los clientes mayores. El vecino que media resume las dos posturas: «Por un lado, el barrio gana en calma; por otro lado, el reparto necesita su horario. Propongo que la calle cierre solo por la tarde.»
stimuli.translation: On the neighbourhood landing, Vega and César argue about the pedestrian street. Vega says the street should be pedestrian in the afternoons: the children play calmly and the terraces fill up. César asks for one loading hour in the morning and short parking spaces for elderly customers. The neighbour who mediates sums up both positions: 'On the one hand, the neighbourhood gains calm; on the other, the deliveries need their schedule. I propose that the street close only in the afternoon.'

pairs.target: En mi opinión, el centro debería ser peatonal por la tarde.
pairs.meaning: In my opinion, the centre should be pedestrian in the afternoon.

pairs.target: Creo que la plaza ganaría en vida, porque la gente pasea sin ruido.
pairs.meaning: I think the square would gain life, because people stroll without noise.

pairs.target: Aunque el reparto se complica, una hora de descarga lo resuelve.
pairs.meaning: Although delivery gets harder, one loading hour solves it.

pairs.target: Sin embargo, sin horarios claros, el problema vuelve.
pairs.meaning: However, without clear schedules, the problem comes back.

pairs.target: En cambio, los comercios ganan clientes que pasean.
pairs.meaning: By contrast, the shops gain customers who stroll.

stimuli.body: En mi opinión, el centro de la ciudad debería cerrar al tráfico por la tarde. Creo que la plaza se llenaría de terrazas, porque la gente pasea cuando no hay ruido. Aunque los comercios necesitan aparcamiento, una hora de descarga por la mañana les bastaría. Sin embargo, sin un horario claro, el reparto se complica otra vez.
stimuli.translation: In my opinion, the city centre should close to traffic in the afternoon. I think the square would fill with terraces, because people stroll when there is no noise. Although the shops need parking, one loading hour in the morning would be enough for them. However, without a clear schedule, deliveries get complicated again.

stimuli.body:
After the meeting, the neighbourhood association asks each neighbour for a short voice note with their own argued take on the street decision. Your mission:
— Open with your stance: En mi opinión, … / Creo que…
— Give two reasons: Porque…
— Concede a point: Aunque…
— Answer it: Sin embargo… / En cambio… / No obstante…
— Close with the summary: En resumen, …
Record your take at the say step and compare it with the model — the judgement is yours.
stimuli.translation: Tras la reunión, la asociación del barrio pide a cada vecino una nota de voz corta con su propia postura sobre la decisión de la calle. Tu misión: abrir con tu postura con en mi opinión, … o creo que …, dar dos razones con porque …, conceder un punto con aunque …, responderlo con sin embargo …, en cambio … o no obstante …, y cerrar con el resumen con en resumen, …. Graba tu postura en el paso de hablar y compárala con el modelo: el juicio es tuyo.

activities.body: It is 10 a.m. in Madrid. You find a seat at a café, and the server comes over. Greet them, ask for un café, and thank them when it arrives. Read the three lines below, then try the exchange yourself.

activities.prompt: The server reaches your table. How do you greet them?
hints: The server spoke to you first, so you answer with a greeting — the one-word line that means 'hello'.
activities.feedback: Hola opens the exchange.

activities.prompt: Build the order: A coffee, please.
hints: The request starts with the article un, then the drink café, and por favor closes it — one line: Un café, por favor.
activities.feedback: Un café, por favor. Keep the request together as one line.

activities.prompt: The cup reaches your table. What do you say?
hints: The order is over and the coffee has arrived — pick the line that closes the exchange by thanking the server.
activities.feedback: Gracias closes the exchange.

activities.prompt: Say the order once in your head. Then write in Spanish: A coffee, please.
hints: It is the same three-word line you just built: un ('a') + café + por favor.
activities.feedback: You wrote the order without the tiles.

errors.explanation: The request needs the small un ('a') in front of café: Un café, por favor.
Por favor is the polite part that makes the request courteous — keep it: Un café, por favor.
Porfavor is not one word — por favor is two separate words.

activities.prompt: Match the three lines you used to their meanings.
hints: Each Spanish line has exactly one English twin — Gracias is the one that means 'thank you'.
activities.feedback: You can recognize the whole exchange.

activities.prompt: Write the three lines in order: Hello. / A coffee, please. / Thank you.
hints: Follow the order of the mission: greet first (Hola.), then the request (Un café, por favor.), then thank the server (Gracias.).
activities.feedback: You greeted, ordered, and thanked the server.

answers: Hola. Un café, por favor. Gracias.

errors.explanation: The polite request keeps por favor: Un café, por favor.
'A coffee' needs its article un in front of café.

activities.body: You are at the counter in Madrid. Listen to the short café exchange: the customer orders, the server answers, the customer decides. You can play it again and again, and the transcript sits below the player.

activities.prompt: Where is this conversation happening?
hints: The exchange opens with an order — un café, por favor — a line that only makes sense at the counter of a café. The bakery and the supermarket never come up.
activities.feedback: The conversation happens at a café: the customer orders un café and settles how to take it.

activities.prompt: What does the customer order?
hints: The first line of the exchange is the order. It names the drink you practiced in this mission's opening step — the one that falls between the greeting and por favor.
activities.feedback: The customer orders un café — the same drink from the mission's opening lines.

activities.prompt: Does the customer drink the coffee here or take it away?
hints: The server asks the question, and the customer answers it in the last line — the answer that ends with gracias.
activities.feedback: The customer stays: para tomar aquí, gracias — he drinks the coffee at the café instead of taking it away.

activities.prompt: The server is waiting. Order politely in Spanish: A coffee, please.

activities.body: One common way to introduce yourself is Me llamo Ana (‘My name is Ana’); literally, it means ‘I call myself Ana.’ Mi nombre es Ana is possible too. To ask someone else, say ¿Cómo te llamas? Both the small pronoun (me → te) and the verb ending (llamo → llamas) change. You can also introduce yourself with Soy Ana (‘I am Ana’).

activities.prompt: Me llamo Ana and Soy Ana both give a name. Which one uses the verb that literally means 'I call myself'?
hints: The reflexive verb is llamarse — the option built on me llamo is the one that literally says 'I call myself'.
activities.feedback: Me llamo Ana is the reflexive form — 'I call myself Ana'. Soy Ana uses ser ('to be'), and ¿Cómo te llamas? is the question.

activities.prompt: Ask a classmate their name with the question whose pronoun changes to te.
hints: It starts with ¿Cómo ('how'), then the pronoun te, then the verb llamas — the question form of the same verb from Me llamo.
activities.feedback: The verb is the same one as in Me llamo, but the pronoun turns into te when it points at the person you are speaking to.

errors.explanation: That is the self-introduction, not a question. Pointing at the other person turns the pronoun into te and the verb into llamas: ¿Cómo te llamas?
Me is for yourself; when you ask someone else the pronoun becomes te: ¿Cómo te llamas?
That is a word-for-word translation from English. Spanish asks 'how do you call yourself': ¿Cómo te llamas?

activities.prompt: Read the exchange. Which short word tells you the first speaker is talking about herself?
hints: Look at the first speaker's line: the two-letter word right before the verb llamo is the reflexive pronoun pointing back at Ana.
activities.feedback: Me is the reflexive pronoun: it turns the verb llamarse back on the person speaking. The other introduction uses soy instead.

errors.explanation: Soy is the verb of the other introduction ('I am Leo') — it has no reflexive pronoun. The first speaker's pronoun is the two-letter word before llamo.
Llamo is the verb, not the pronoun. The short word that turns it back on the speaker is me, right before it.

activities.prompt: A neighbour introduces herself to you. Give the two-word Spanish reply that closes an introduction.
hints: It is the fixed phrase from the examples that means 'nice to meet you' — two words, no verb, and it works for any speaker.
activities.feedback: Mucho gusto closes an introduction, and the sentence needs no pronoun.

errors.explanation: De nada means 'you're welcome' — it answers gracias, not an introduction. The two-word closer is Mucho gusto.
Encantada is also a polite closer (it agrees with the speaker's gender), but the two-word form this lesson teaches is Mucho gusto.

activities.prompt: The words are jumbled. Build the reflexive sentence that gives Ana's name.
hints: The reflexive pronoun comes first, then the verb, then the name: Me + llamo + Ana.
activities.feedback: Me llamo Ana puts the reflexive pronoun first, then the verb, then the name.

activities.prompt: A classmate has introduced herself. Introduce yourself the same way, as Ana, using the verb that needs a pronoun.
hints: Use the same three words you just built: the pronoun Me, then llamo, then the name Ana — the pronoun cannot be left out.
activities.feedback: Say the whole reflexive phrase; leaving out me would leave the verb belonging to nobody.

errors.explanation: The reflexive verb needs its pronoun: without me, the verb belongs to nobody. Say Me llamo Ana.
Soy Ana uses plain 'to be'. The prompt asks for the reflexive form with its pronoun: Me llamo Ana.

activities.body: Quiero means 'I want', and in a café it can sound blunt. Spanish softens the same verb into quisiera, 'I would like', and that ending is the whole difference: Quisiera un café, por favor. The article un does not change with the drink — Quisiera un té, por favor — so only the noun moves. Keep the accents: café and té each carry one, and por favor is the phrase that turns the request into a courteous one.

activities.prompt: Quiero and quisiera are the same verb. Which request is the softened, polite one?
hints: The polite form is the longer one that starts with Quis- and ends in -a — it sounds like 'key-syeh-rah'.
activities.feedback: Quisiera gives the verb a conditional ending, and that is what makes the request courteous. Quiero is the blunt form.

activities.prompt: Ask for tea politely, using the softened verb rather than quiero.
hints: Same frame as the café request: start with Quisiera, then un té (with the accent on té), and close with por favor.
activities.feedback: Same polite frame, tea instead of coffee: Quisiera un té, por favor, with the accent on té.

errors.explanation: Quiero is the blunt 'I want'. The softened form is quisiera — the same verb with the conditional ending.
Té carries an accent — without it, te means 'you', not 'tea'.
Keep the polite closer: Quisiera un té, por favor.

activities.prompt: Read the café exchange. How many drinks does the customer order?
hints: Count everything the customer asks for: the té in the first line, plus the extra drink added with 'y un café también' ('and a coffee too').
activities.feedback: The customer asks for a té and then adds un café, so two drinks in all.

errors.explanation: The first line asks for a té, but the customer comes back and adds un café too (y un café también) — two drinks in all.
There is more than one order: a té, then an added un café — two drinks in all.

activities.prompt: What does this café line mean in English: Quisiera un café, por favor.
hints: Quisiera is the polite 'I would like' (like 'I'd like'), un café is 'a coffee', and por favor is 'please'.
activities.feedback: Quisiera is 'I would like', and por favor supplies the 'please'.

answers: I would like a coffee, please.

errors.explanation: Quiero would mean 'I want'. The line uses quisiera, the polite 'I would like'.
The line keeps the polite verb at the front: 'I would like a coffee, please'.

activities.prompt: Put the words in order to build the polite request for one coffee.
hints: The polite verb comes first (Quisiera), then the drink with its article (un café), then the two-word closer (por favor).
activities.feedback: Quisiera opens it, the drink follows with un, and por favor finishes the request.

activities.prompt: You reach the counter and want a coffee. Make the short polite request, without the verb.
hints: Drop the verb entirely — simply name the drink with its article and add por favor: Un café, por favor.
activities.feedback: Un café, por favor — the short request drops quisiera but keeps por favor.

errors.explanation: The request needs its article: 'a coffee' is un café, por favor.
Keep the polite closer por favor — it is what makes the short request courteous.

activities.body: Spanish counts one to ten straight. The stretch that surprises English speakers is the twenties: veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés, written as one word, the same way dieciséis and diecisiete glue their parts together. The separate y arrives only at thirty-one, treinta y uno. Because the number agrees with its noun, one is un with a masculine café and una with a feminine manzana.

activities.prompt: Three is hiding inside veintitrés, glued to veinte. Which Spanish word is it?
hints: Split veintitrés in half: veinti- carries the 'twenty', and the glued tail holds the number you already know from one to ten.
activities.feedback: Tres is three. The twenties simply glue a number onto veinte, so veintitrés is twenty-three.

activities.prompt: Read the price board. How much is the tea?
hints: Find the line that starts with Té — its price is the second one on the board: tres euros.
activities.feedback: The board prices tea at tres euros. Dos and tres behave here exactly as they did when you counted.

errors.explanation: Dos euros is the price of the coffee (Café: dos euros). The tea line reads Té: tres euros.

activities.prompt: Put the Spanish words in order to ask the price of one coffee.
hints: The inverted question mark opens the sentence with ¿Cuánto, the verb cuesta follows, then the drink with its article: un café.
activities.feedback: ¿Cuánto cuesta? is the price question as a unit, and the upside-down question mark opens the sentence. Un café follows it.

activities.prompt: Say in Spanish: Two apples, please.
hints: Dos works for any noun, manzanas is the plural of 'apple', and the polite closer por favor ends the line.
activities.feedback: Manzanas is feminine plural, so 'one' would be una, but two is dos either way, only the word for one changes with the noun.

errors.explanation: With dos ('two') the noun is plural: dos manzanas.
Una means 'one' — the prompt asks for two, which is dos: Dos manzanas, por favor.
End the request politely with por favor: Dos manzanas, por favor.

activities.prompt: Think: a fruit seller has one apple but no sign. Ask the price in Spanish, then write the question.
hints: Use the same price question from this lesson — ¿Cuánto cuesta — and make 'one apple' agree with the feminine noun: una manzana.
activities.feedback: One apple is una manzana, with the feminine una. The price question itself never changes.

errors.explanation: Manzana is feminine, so 'one' must be una, not un: ¿Cuánto cuesta una manzana?
The question needs the article before the noun: una manzana.

activities.prompt: Three of these give a direction; the fourth is asking. Which single word is the asking one?
hints: The asking word carries a written accent and means 'where'. The other three — izquierda, derecha, recto — tell you a way to go, and none of them asks anything.
activities.feedback: Dónde means where, and the written accent is there because the word is asking. Quién does the same job for a person, qué for a thing.

activities.prompt: Put the Spanish words in order to ask where the station is.
hints: The question opens with the asking word ¿Dónde, then the verb está, then the article la, then the place estación — exactly the order from the exchange you read.
activities.feedback: The question opens with ¿ and its asking word dónde, and estar supplies está. Estación is feminine, so its article is la.

activities.prompt: Ask in Spanish where the bathroom is. Baño is masculine.
hints: Keep the skeleton from the station question — ¿Dónde está + article + place. The prompt hands you the article: baño is masculine, so it takes el.
activities.feedback: Only the noun and its article change inside ¿Dónde está?; el marks the masculine baño. The accent on dónde stays, because the word is still asking.

errors.explanation: The article el has to sit between the verb and the place: ¿Dónde está el baño?
Location takes estar, not ser — a place is where it is: ¿Dónde está el baño?
The prompt marks baño as masculine, so its article is el, not la: ¿Dónde está el baño?
Estás means 'you are'. The question asks where the bathroom is — third person está: ¿Dónde está el baño?

activities.prompt: Complete the directions: Todo recto, luego a la ___
hints: Todo recto comes first; luego means 'then'. The turn that follows is to the left: a la izquierda.
activities.feedback: Izquierda is left. Derecha is the opposite, and a la is fixed in front of both of them.

segments.text: Complete the directions: Todo recto, luego a la

errors.explanation: Derecha is 'right'. The passerby said to turn left after going straight: a la izquierda.
Direction phrases use the fixed feminine form a la izquierda; izquierdo appears with masculine nouns (el lado izquierdo).

activities.prompt: Soften the question by putting Perdone in front: ¿Dónde está la estación?
hints: Perdone goes ahead of the question, comma after it — the question itself stays exactly as it was, with its accent on dónde.
activities.feedback: Perdone goes ahead of the question and a comma separates it. The accent on dónde stays, because it is still the word asking where.

errors.explanation: The polite opener Perdone must come first — strangers get that courtesy: Perdone, ¿dónde está la estación?
Perdona is the informal tú form. For a stranger use the formal Perdone.

activities.prompt: Spanish fences a question with two marks, the first of them upside down. Which of these is asking the price?
hints: The price question is cuánto + cuesta: ¿Cuánto cuesta? Cómo and dónde ask how and where — the money word is cuánto.
activities.feedback: ¿Cuánto cuesta? is the price question: cuánto asks how much, cuesta comes from costar, and both marks are obligatory.

activities.prompt: At a café in Seville you are pricing one coffee only. Ask the question.
hints: Cuesta is costar for ONE thing — un café. Open with ¿Cuánto (accent on the o); several things would flip the verb to cuestan.
activities.feedback: Cuesta is singular because one coffee is being priced; for several the verb would turn into cuestan.

errors.explanation: Cuestan fits several things; one coffee keeps the singular cuesta.
A specific coffee takes its article: un café — ¿Cuánto cuesta un café?
Costar is the infinitive; the question needs the conjugated form — cuesta.
Cuánto es asks the total; pricing one item takes costar: ¿Cuánto cuesta un café?

activities.prompt: You think the price is fair. Turn «Es caro.» into its opposite.
hints: The opposite of expensive starts with no before the verb: Es caro → No es caro. Spanish pins the no to the front of the verb, never the end.
activities.feedback: No goes before the verb es; Spanish never lets the negation wander to the end of the sentence.

errors.explanation: The no stands before the verb: No es caro — Spanish never tucks it after es.
Barato is the opposite word, but the drill is the negation of caro — No es caro.
The negation pins itself to the verb: No es caro, not 'No caro es'.

activities.prompt: Dinner in Madrid is over and you want to settle up. Ask the waiter for the bill.
hints: The bill is feminine: la cuenta. Pair it with por favor and the request stays polite: La cuenta, por favor.
activities.feedback: Cuenta is feminine, so it takes la, and por favor is what keeps the request polite.

errors.explanation: Cuenta is feminine — la cuenta, never el cuenta.
The bare demand reads brusque; the polite line pairs it with por favor: La cuenta, por favor.
The politeness marker is por favor — the by-your-leave: La cuenta, por favor.

activities.body: Spanish weekdays are the Roman sky turned into a calendar: lunes is the moon, martes Mars, miércoles Mercury, jueves Jupiter and viernes Venus. Then the naming breaks — sábado comes from the Sabbath and domingo from the Lord’s day. The days are masculine and lower-case, and Spanish needs no separate word for ‘on’: the article el carries it, as in el lunes. Watch out, too: mañana is tomorrow, while la mañana is the morning.

activities.prompt: Your Madrid phone writes a label above the date. Tap the label for today.
hints: Hoy is the label for today. Mañana is tomorrow, lunes a weekday and semana the week — the phone's label for the current day is hoy.
activities.feedback: That is hoy. The decoys mean tomorrow, Monday and the week.

activities.prompt: Build the Spanish sentence for on Monday I work; the article carries the on.
hints: The article El carries the 'on' and sits first, then the day lunes, then the verb trabajo: El lunes trabajo.
activities.feedback: El sits in front of the day and means on: el lunes, on Monday.

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish for on Mondays, meaning every Monday: ___ lunes trabajo.
hints: The plural article Los makes it 'on Mondays' — every Monday, a habit. El would mean one single Monday; the prompt says every Monday.
activities.feedback: Spanish uses the plural article for a repeated day: los lunes, on Mondays.

segments.text: Complete the Spanish for on Mondays, meaning every Monday:

errors.explanation: El lunes means one single Monday. 'On Mondays', every Monday, needs the plural: los lunes.
Lunes is masculine, so the plural article is los, never las.
La is feminine and singular; the repeated-day habit needs the masculine plural: los lunes.

activities.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: today is Friday.
hints: Dates and days ride ser, not estar: Hoy es … Then the day, lower-case as the intro taught: viernes.
activities.feedback: Hoy es plus the day. Viernes still carries the name of Venus.

errors.explanation: Days and dates ride ser, not estar — the day is what it is: Hoy es viernes.
The prompt asks for Friday — hoy es viernes. Martes is the day of Mars, not the answer.
The time word hoy leads in Spanish: Hoy es viernes.

activities.prompt: Give the English meaning: El lunes trabajo.
hints: El in front of a weekday carries the 'on' — there is no separate word for it. Read the article with the day, then the work: On Monday I work.
activities.feedback: There is no separate word for on here; the article el does that work in front of the day.

errors.explanation: The little 'on' is hiding in the article el — 'on Monday' is part of the sentence: On Monday I work.
Trabajo is the present 'I work'. The sentence is about a habit, not a finished past: On Monday I work.
The article el means 'on' here; English needs no extra article with the day: I work on Monday.

activities.prompt: Five Spanish weekdays carry the name of a planet or a god. Which pair leaves that company?
hints: The prompt asks which pair does NOT follow the sky names. Sábado came from the Sabbath and domingo from the Lord's day — those two broke away, so they are the odd pair out.
activities.feedback: Sábado comes from the Sabbath and domingo from the Lord's day; lunes to viernes are the old sky names.

activities.prompt: Read the week. Which day does the passage name after the moon?
hints: The passage's first line names the day: El lunes es el día de la Luna. Which weekday is the day of the moon?
activities.feedback: The first line says it: el lunes is the day of la Luna, the moon.

errors.explanation: Martes is the day the writer works — the moon day is lunes.
Viernes is the rest day; the moon gets lunes: El lunes es el día de la Luna.
The moon is what the day is NAMED after — the question asks for the day itself: lunes.

activities.prompt: One letter separates the Spanish words for brother and sister. Which of these four is the sister?
hints: Sister is hermana — hermano with an a — and the article agrees: la for the feminine sister, el for the brother.
activities.feedback: Hermana is the sister; the -a ending marks her feminine, as -o marks hermano. Padres is the pair of parents, and la familia is the household.

activities.prompt: Hermana is feminine and keeps the same article as the subject. Choose the line that correctly says I have a sister.
hints: Hermana is feminine: una pairs with hermana. Un (masculine) and unos (plural) both clash with the one feminine sister.
activities.feedback: Una hermana keeps the feminine article una; un hermana and unos hermana are the two ways learners get this wrong.

activities.prompt: You are describing the one brother you have. Predict the form before you write it: I have a brother.
hints: Tener breaks the pattern in the I form: tengo, never *tene. One brother is un hermano — singular, no mis: Tengo un hermano.
activities.feedback: Tener is irregular, so the I form is tengo and never tene: Tengo un hermano.

errors.explanation: Tener's I form is irregular: tengo, never tene.
Hermano is masculine, so it takes un: un hermano. Una would demand the feminine hermana.
Unos hermanos says several brothers; the prompt has the one brother — un hermano.

activities.prompt: Read what Ana wrote about her family. Which city are the parents still in?
hints: The parents are the ones who stayed: mis padres siguen viviendo en Madrid — the closing sentence. Max works in Seville, Ana studies in Valencia.
activities.feedback: The brother and sister are in Seville and Valencia; the closing sentence keeps the parents in Madrid.

errors.explanation: Sevilla is where the brother Max works; the parents are the ones who stayed — Madrid.
Valencia is where the sister Ana studies; the parents still live in Madrid.
En Sevilla is the brother's city; the closing line keeps the parents in Madrid.

activities.prompt: Make the sentence talk about two sisters instead of one: Tengo una hermana.
hints: Pluralize both ends: una becomes dos, and hermana takes its -s: hermanas. Tengo dos hermanas.
activities.feedback: The plural adds -s to hermana, and una becomes dos: Tengo dos hermanas.

errors.explanation: Two sisters need the plural noun: hermanas, with its -s.
Una is singular-one; with the plural sisters you count dos (or more): dos hermanas.
Hermanos is masculine — brothers or a mixed group; the two SISTERS are dos hermanas.

activities.body: You already know the polite café request from «At the café». Today you build it yourself, block by block. Every polite request in this lesson is made of the same blocks: the softened verb quisiera, the drink with un, and por favor at the end. Notice the order — the verb always opens, and por favor always closes.

activities.prompt: Build the polite request for one coffee, starting with the softened verb.
hints: The frame never changes: the softened verb Quisiera opens, then un + the drink, and por favor closes. Start with Quisiera and the rest falls into place.
activities.feedback: Quisiera opens, un café names the drink, and por favor closes — that order never changes.

activities.prompt: Build the polite request for one tea.
hints: Same frame as the coffee: Quisiera opens, then un té — té with its accent — and por favor closes the request.
activities.feedback: Same frame, new drink — and the accent on té stays.

activities.prompt: The verb is missing. Complete the polite request.
hints: The blank is the softened opener that sits alone before un café — the quisiera form, not the blunt quiero.
activities.feedback: Quisiera is the softened form of quiero — the polite opener.

errors.explanation: Quiero states the wish bluntly; the polite frame softens it to Quisiera — the quisiera form, not quiero.
Quisieras adds the -s for tú (you); the request about yourself takes the I-form Quisiera.
Quería is a past 'I wanted'; the polite opener here is the conditional Quisiera.

activities.prompt: Which of these is the polite way to ask for coffee?
hints: The polite coffee request needs BOTH the softened verb and the right drink: Quisiera opens, café follows un, por favor closes. One decoy swaps in tea and another moves the verb after the drink.
activities.feedback: Quisiera softens the verb, quiero is blunt, and word order matters.

activities.prompt: Build the short polite request — no verb, just the drink.
hints: No verb today: Un + the drink comes first, and por favor still closes the phrase — Un café, por favor.
activities.feedback: Drop the verb and the request still works: Un café, por favor.

activities.prompt: Type the polite request for one tea.
hints: Type the full frame from the tiles: Quisiera opens, then un té — the accent on é is part of the word — then por favor.
activities.feedback: Quisiera un té, por favor. — the accent on té is part of the spelling.

errors.explanation: Te without the accent is the pronoun 'you'; tea is té, and that accent is part of the word.
Quiero is the blunt form; the polite request softens the verb — Quisiera un té, por favor.
The frame order is fixed: Quisiera, then un té, then por favor — and té keeps its accent.
The prompt asks for tea, not coffee: un té. Keep the frame, change the drink.

activities.prompt: Fill the blank, and mind the accent — the drink is tea.
hints: The drink is tea — té with the accent. Te without it is a different word (the pronoun 'you').
activities.feedback: Té keeps its accent. Without it, te means something else entirely.

errors.explanation: Te without the accent means 'you'; tea is té — keep the accent on the é.
The prompt says the drink is tea — té. Café was the earlier step's drink.

activities.prompt: A friend joins you and wants tea too. Build the polite request for one tea — from memory.
hints: From memory: the softened verb Quisiera, then un té (accented), then por favor — the same three blocks you used with coffee, tea swapped in.
activities.feedback: You built it without the frame in front of you. That is the point of today.

activities.body: A friend is waiting for you at a café across town, and your phone is dead. Your mission has four parts: ask where the café is, follow the directions you are given, order a coffee politely, and ask for the bill. Everything you need was taught in «Asking the way», «At the café», and «Prices and paying». Read the mission card, then go.

activities.prompt: You stop a passerby. Which question asks where the café is?
hints: Dónde asks 'where' and opens the question; your target is the café: ¿Dónde está el café? The price question ¿Cuánto cuesta? belongs to the bill, later in the mission.
activities.feedback: Dónde asks 'where' — and it keeps its accent because it is a question.

activities.prompt: Complete the question.
hints: The blank holds the asking word for 'where' — capital D, with the accent you learned in «Asking the way».
activities.feedback: Dónde with the accent asks 'where' — the directions lesson used it with the station, and it works for the café too.

errors.explanation: Qué means 'what' or 'that' — the place question wants the where-word: ¿Dónde está el café?
Cómo is 'how'. Asking where the café is needs dónde: ¿Dónde está el café?

activities.prompt: The passerby says: «A la izquierda, luego todo recto.» What do you do first?
hints: Luego means 'then'. The direction first on the list is the one you do first: turn left, then go straight ahead.
activities.feedback: A la izquierda is 'to the left', and luego tells you the straight part comes second.

options.text: Turn left, then go straight ahead.
Turn right, then go straight ahead.
Go straight ahead, then turn left.

activities.prompt: The next turn is to the right. Complete the direction.
hints: The next turn is to the right — 'to the right' is a la derecha, the twin of a la izquierda.
activities.feedback: A la derecha — right. The directions lesson paired it against a la izquierda.

errors.explanation: Izquierda is 'left' — the turn you already took. This one is to the right: derecha.
The fixed direction phrase is a la derecha, with the feminine form; derecho is the masculine word used with nouns (el lado derecho).

activities.prompt: You found the café. Order one coffee, politely.
hints: The polite order goes Quisiera + un + café, and por favor closes it — the same frame you practiced at the café.
activities.feedback: Quisiera wins again. But the server shakes her head — the coffee is finished!

activities.prompt: No coffee left. What do you order instead?
hints: Keep the exact polite frame and swap the drink: tea is té — Quisiera un té, por favor.
activities.feedback: Tea saves the mission — same polite frame, and the accent on té stays.

activities.prompt: Mission nearly complete. Ask for the bill, the way «Prices and paying» taught you.
